title: Lesson — 20 November
description: Your words for 20 November: idioms and nouns for strong feelings, listening in and overhearing, and words for talking about spoken-word poetry.

items.translation: выводить кого-то из себя, доводить до белого каления
items.definition: to make someone very annoyed, especially by doing something again and again
items.example: My neighbour's dog barks all night and it [drives me up the wall].
items.exampleRu: Соседская собака лает всю ночь, и это доводит меня до белого каления.
items.pattern: sth drives sb up the wall · be driving sb up the wall
items.trap: It's 'up the wall', not 'on the wall' or 'to the wall'.

items.definition: to feel very nervous or excited before something important
items.example: I always [have butterflies in my stomach] before a job interview.
items.exampleRu: Перед собеседованием у меня всегда бабочки в животе.
items.pattern: have/get butterflies (in your stomach) before sth
items.trap: Always plural 'butterflies', and 'in your stomach', not 'on'. In English it's usually nerves, not only love.

items.translation: рвать на себе волосы (от отчаяния или злости)
items.definition: to be extremely worried, angry or frustrated about something
items.example: After the third failed attempt to install the printer, I was [tearing my hair out].
items.exampleRu: После третьей неудачной попытки установить принтер я был готов рвать на себе волосы.
collocations: tear your hair out over sth
make sb want to tear their hair out
items.pattern: be tearing your hair out (over sth)
items.trap: 'Hair' is uncountable: not 'hairs'. Past: tear – tore – torn.

items.definition: to laugh a lot and for a long time (informal)
items.example: His story about the wedding was so funny that we were [killing ourselves laughing].
items.exampleRu: Его история про свадьбу была такой смешной, что мы умирали со смеху.
items.trap: Use the -ing form 'laughing': not 'from laughing' or 'with laugh' (calques of «со смеху»).

items.definition: to suddenly become very angry and show it
items.example: I [lost my temper] when the delivery was late for the third time.
items.exampleRu: Я вспылил, когда доставка опоздала в третий раз.
items.trap: Not 'went out of myself' (calque of «вышел из себя»). 'Temper', not 'temperature'.

items.definition: to be nervous and unable to relax, usually because you are waiting for something
items.example: Everyone [was on edge] while we waited for the exam results.
items.exampleRu: Все были на взводе, пока мы ждали результатов экзамена.
items.trap: No article: 'on edge'. 'On the edge' means physically at the edge of something.

items.definition: to be angry with yourself because you made a silly mistake or missed a chance
items.example: I could [kick myself] for forgetting her birthday again.
items.exampleRu: Я так ругаю себя за то, что опять забыл про её день рождения.
items.trap: Use the reflexive 'myself/yourself', not 'kick me'.

items.translation: быть настоящей головной болью, сильно раздражать
items.definition: to be very annoying or cause a lot of trouble (informal)
items.example: Finding a parking space in the city centre [is a real pain].
items.exampleRu: Найти парковку в центре города — настоящая головная боль.
collocations: a real pain in the neck
be a pain to do sth
items.pattern: sth/sb is a real pain · it's a pain to + verb
items.trap: «Головная боль» in this sense = 'a pain' or 'a headache', never 'an ache'.
accepted: a real pain in the neck

items.definition: the feeling of being annoyed
items.example: To my [annoyance], the train was cancelled again.
items.exampleRu: К моему раздражению, поезд снова отменили.
items.pattern: to sb's annoyance · annoyance at/with sth
items.trap: The noun ends in -ance: annoy → annoyance (not 'annoyment').

items.definition: a strong feeling of being very annoyed and wanting to shout or hurt someone
items.example: She couldn't hide her [anger] when she saw the bill.
items.exampleRu: Она не смогла скрыть злость, когда увидела счёт.
items.trap: 'Anger' is the noun, 'angry' is the adjective: 'I felt anger' but 'I was angry'.

items.definition: the state of feeling nervous or worried
items.example: He tried to hide his [nervousness] by talking very fast.
items.exampleRu: Он пытался скрыть волнение, говоря очень быстро.
items.trap: Not 'nervosity': the noun is nervous + -ness.

items.definition: the feeling of being ready to do anything because a situation is so bad
items.example: In [desperation], I called my old teacher for help.
items.exampleRu: В отчаянии я позвонил своему старому учителю за помощью.
items.trap: Spelling: desp-e-ration (like 'desperate'). 'Despair' is giving up hope; 'desperation' is when you try anything.

items.definition: the feeling you have when something is funny
items.example: Much to our [amusement], the dog stole a sausage from the table.
items.exampleRu: К нашему веселью, собака стащила со стола сосиску.
items.trap: Spelling: keep the 'e' — amuse + ment = amusement.

items.definition: to secretly listen to other people's conversation on purpose
items.example: My little sister always tries to [listen in on] my phone calls.
items.exampleRu: Моя младшая сестра всегда пытается подслушать мои телефонные разговоры.
items.trap: You do it on purpose. If you hear something by accident, use 'overhear'.

items.definition: to hear what other people are saying without them knowing and usually by accident
items.example: I [overheard] two colleagues talking about my promotion.
items.exampleRu: Я случайно услышал, как двое коллег обсуждали моё повышение.
items.pattern: overhear sb doing/say sth · overhear – overheard – overheard
items.trap: Irregular: overheard, not 'overheared'. Usually by accident (unlike 'listen in on').

items.definition: a poem written to be performed out loud to an audience
items.example: At the school festival she performed a [spoken-word poem] about her grandmother.
items.exampleRu: На школьном фестивале она исполнила стихотворение о своей бабушке.
items.trap: 'Spoken' is the past participle: not 'speaking-word' or 'speak-word'.

items.definition: a person who writes poems
items.example: Pushkin is the [poet] every Russian child learns about at school.
items.exampleRu: Пушкин — поэт, которого каждый российский школьник изучает в школе.
items.trap: Don't mix them up: a poet writes a poem; poetry is poems in general.

items.definition: something that gives you new ideas or makes you want to create or do something
items.example: The poet finds [inspiration] in ordinary conversations on the bus.
items.exampleRu: Поэт находит вдохновение в обычных разговорах в автобусе.
items.trap: The noun is 'inspiration'; the verb is 'inspire'. Not 'inspirement'.

items.definition: words that end with the same sound, like 'cat' and 'hat'
items.example: 'Moon' and 'June' are [rhyming words].
items.exampleRu: «Moon» и «June» — рифмующиеся слова.
items.trap: Rhyme /raɪm/ (рифма) is not rhythm /ˈrɪðəm/ (ритм).

items.definition: one part of a word that has one vowel sound
items.example: The word 'banana' has three [syllables].
items.exampleRu: В слове «banana» три слога.
items.trap: Stress is on the first syllable: SYL-la-ble. Spelling: double 'l', 'y' after s.

items.definition: words that are said more strongly than others to show they are important
items.example: In a spoken-word poem, the [stressed words] carry the meaning and the rhythm.
items.exampleRu: В устном стихотворении выделенные слова несут смысл и ритм.
items.pattern: stress/emphasise a word · put emphasis on sth
items.trap: 'Stressed' (ударный) is not 'stressful' (напряжённый). American spelling: emphasized.

items.definition: saying or doing the same thing again, often for effect in a poem or speech
items.example: The poet uses [repetition]: the line 'I am still here' comes back five times.
items.exampleRu: Поэт использует повторение: строка «I am still here» звучит пять раз.
items.trap: Spelling changes from 'repeat': rep-e-tition, not 'repeatition'.

items.definition: words, sounds or actions that show how someone feels
items.example: Crying and laughing are natural [expressions of emotion].
items.exampleRu: Плач и смех — естественные выражения эмоций.
items.trap: Use 'of': 'expressions of emotion', not 'with' or 'expressing of'.
